newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Democrats welcome art portfolio decision.
newsitem.headline: Australia Democrats welcome art portfolio decision.

text.p: The Australian Democrats minor party on Tuesday welcomed the Australian government's decision not to sell its art collection, but questioned its long-term objectives.
The collection is kept by Artbank, an official agency, to lease to government offices. Arts Minister Richard Alston announced on Sunday it would be kept in public hands.
But he said the government wanted to enhance its profitability through widening its revenue base by showing the collection around Australia.
Until now, Artbank had concentrated its activities in the states of New South Wales and Western Australia, and the Australian Capital Territory.
But the Democrats said the extra exposure would cost more than it could raise.
"Artbank already achieves its objectives at no on-going cost to the government," Democrats arts spokeswoman Lyn Allison said in a statement.
"The minister's insistence that it should make a profit and show around the country doesn't stack up."
The portfolio -- completely separate from the National Gallery's collection -- is valued at about A$11 million.
The Liberal-National government has sold several government assets since taking office in March last year.
